instruction: In Y22-2119-assign4.docx, make all italic terms stand out clearly by changing their font size to 14pt and making them bold. Save the file when done.

llm_judge_reasons: The getter correctly downloads the docx file and uses python-docx to scan italic runs in all paragraphs, checking both font size (14pt) and bold status.
The metric correctly implements partial credit: 0.5 for all italic runs being 14pt, 0.5 for all italic runs being bold, matching both instruction requirements.
The negative control (do-nothing agent) would correctly fail because italic runs in paragraphs would remain 12pt and not bold.
The evaluator covers both sub-goals from the instruction: font size 14pt AND bold formatting for all italic terms.
Minor issue: getter only scans doc.paragraphs and misses italic runs in tables, headers, footers, or text boxes. For a typical academic assignment docx this is low risk.
Minor issue: run.italic in python-docx returns None (not True) for inherited italic formatting, so style-inherited italic runs could be missed.
Minor issue: run.font.size returns None for inherited size, which would fail the == 14.0 check even if the run visually displays at 14pt via style inheritance.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider also iterating over table cells: for table in doc.tables: for row in table.rows: for cell in row.cells: for para in cell.paragraphs: for run in para.runs: ...
Use run.italic is not False instead of run.italic to capture runs where italic is inherited (run.italic returns None for inherited italic).
When checking bold, use run.bold is not False instead of bool(run.bold) to handle inherited bold from style.
